match.reason: The bank point covers measuring GDP, nominal versus real output and GDP per capita, not how leading, coincident and lagging economic indicators move relative to the business cycle, so no existing point teaches this idea.

draft.title: Economic indicators
card: An economic indicator is a statistic that shows how the economy is performing. Indicators are grouped by when they change compared with the economy as a whole.
Leading
changes before the economy does, so it can hint at what is coming. Building approvals are an example.
Coincident
moves at the same time as the economy. Gross domestic product (GDP), the value of goods and services produced, is an example.
Lagging
changes after the economy has already turned. The unemployment rate is an example.
draft.remember: Leading indicators come before the economy, coincident ones move with it, and lagging ones follow.

a.q: Why is the unemployment rate called a lagging indicator?
opts: It usually changes after the economy has turned
It usually changes before the economy turns
It moves at the same time as the economy
It measures only the past year of spending
a.why: Businesses wait until a change in the economy seems lasting before they hire or lay off workers, so unemployment turns after the economy does. It is not leading, because it does not signal a turn in advance.
a.clue: Think about when firms decide to hire or lay off staff.

b.q: In Geelong, building approvals fall for several months in a row, while GDP is still rising. What is the best reading of this?
opts: The economy may be about to slow down
The economy has already begun to slow
The economy is certain to enter a recession
The approvals figure must be a mistake
b.why: Building approvals are a leading indicator, so a fall can hint that the economy will slow. It is only a hint, so it does not prove a recession is certain. GDP is coincident and still shows growth now.
b.clue: A leading indicator points ahead, but it is a hint only.

a.best: It usually changes after the economy has turned

b.best: The economy may be about to slow down

problems.detail: The right option is the only hedged one ('may'). The other three are absolute ('already', 'must', 'certain'), so a student can pick it from its wording alone without knowing what a leading indicator is.
The clue 'it is a hint only' points straight at the one hedged option and gives the answer away.

The question mixes Geelong building approvals with GDP, which is usually a national figure. A fall in one city's approvals does not clearly signal a slowdown in 'the economy'. Using national or Victorian approvals would remove the ambiguity.

b.q: Across Australia, building approvals fall for several months in a row, while GDP is still rising. What does this most likely suggest?
opts: Growth is likely to slow in the months ahead
Growth is likely to have slowed months ago
Growth is likely to speed up in the months ahead
Unemployment is likely to have risen months ago
b.why: Building approvals are a leading indicator, so a fall hints that growth may slow ahead. Growth has not slowed already, because GDP is a coincident indicator and it still shows growth now.
b.clue: Which kind of indicator are building approvals, and which is GDP?
